title: Assistant Briefcase — feature seed and rough PRD
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for a lightweight feature idea: 'Assistant Briefcase' — let end users bundle a concise set of items from an assistant session (prompts, pinned responses, a small memory snapshot, attached files/tools) into a portable package they can re-open across devices or share with teammates.

Motivation / user problem:
- Users want to save and transport a useful slice of an assistant conversation without snapshotting entire history.
- Use cases: handing off a partially-composed task to a coworker, saving a short research pack, exporting a workflow that requires a few tools and a context preseed.
- Current workaround: copy/paste, export full session (heavy), or rely on ephemeral thread links (fragile).

High-level idea:
- UI affordance: "Add to Briefcase" on message/tool outputs and a lightweight "Briefcase" panel in the assistant UI.
- Each briefcase item is typed: message, user-instruction, tool-config (e.g., code runner snippet), small memory snippet (200–800 tokens), attachments (<= 10 MB).
- When opening a briefcase, assistant primes a short context (preface + pinned items) and offers a set of suggested next actions.
- Optional share link or workspace copy for teammates (respecting tenant privacy and Dedicated/Private boundaries).

Key components (MVP):
1) Client UI: briefcase drawer + add/remove on messages; simple list, tags, and short descriptions.
2) Server model: briefcase object stored in user account (hosted) with metadata (created_by, created_at, size, items list).
3) Small context priming: When launched, the assistant prepends a 1–3 message preface derived from briefcase items (configurable max tokens).
4) Export/Share: generate a shareable link (requires tenant opt-in) or team copy (workspace).
5) Permissions & privacy: encryption-at-rest, KMS key reference for Private; sharing toggles (private / team / link).

User stories (examples):
- As a product manager, I want to pin a design brief and two messages into a briefcase so I can hand off to a contractor with enough context to continue work.
- As an engineer, I want to capture a code snippet + tool config to replicate a run later.
- As a support agent, I want to package the last three assistant responses and a note to escalate to L2.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Users can create a briefcase with at least one item and name it.
- Items: message, user note, attachment (max 10MB), memory snippet (max 800 tokens).
- Opening a briefcase primes the assistant with <= 1024 tokens of preface constructed from items.
- Briefcase save/restore works across devices in hosted mode.
- Share link generation creates an access-limited URL and records an audit entry.

Metrics / success signals:
- Activation rate: % of active assistants that create at least one briefcase in 30 days. Target 3% for early adoption.
- Reopen rate: % of briefcases opened at least once after creation. Target 40%.
- Share-to-use ratio: shared briefcases that lead to a new session from recipient. Target 25%.
- Latency: briefcase open priming should not add >50ms median to the first-token latency (server cost should be bounded).

Rollout & scope considerations:
- Phase 0: internal dogfood + SRE test tenants — only create/store, no sharing. Collect telemetry and edge cases (size, attachment types).
- Phase 1: hosted customers opt-in + UI polished. Add share links and workspace copies.
- Phase 2: Dedicated/Private: add KMS control, retention policies, and admin toggles for sharing.

Risks & open questions:
- Cost: storing many briefcases with attachments could become expensive — need TTL and quotas per account.
- Semantic drift: priming from a briefcase could change model output unpredictably — need evals per model variant.
- Privacy: what happens if a briefcase includes PII? Need redaction helpers or confirm dialogs before sharing.
- UX complexity: we must avoid creating another confusing artifact for users to manage (compare with "snapshots" and bookmarks).

Implementation notes / rough infra sketch:
- DB: briefcases table keyed by user_id, tenant_id, created_at, items[]. Items are small records (type, pointer to blob for attachments).
- Storage: attachments in object store with tenant scoping. TTL and size quotas enforced.
- API endpoints: POST /briefcases, GET /briefcases/{id}, POST /briefcases/{id}/open (returns preface tokens and priming plan), POST /briefcases/{id}/share.
- Client: React drawer component + item action on message bubbles; small animation and a "preview preface" modal for transparency.
- Eval plan: set up a small prompt suite that validates that preface + model does not hallucinate immediate identity/data.

Ideas for future iterations (nice-to-have):
- Briefcase templates: allow users to create a typed template (e.g., "handoff", "runbook", "research pack").
- Versioning and diffs for briefcases.
- Programmatic API for team automation (create briefcase from webhook).
- Lightweight encryption for attachments on top of tenant KMS.
- Cross-tenant sharing where a sanitized summary is created for public links.

Unresolved design questions (call out to product/design):
- How granular should "add to briefcase" be? (single message vs selection of messages).
- Should briefcase priming be additive to session context or replace a portion of it?
- Which attachments types cause highest risk (executables, large images)? Block or allow?

Next steps / todo (me):
- 1) Quick mockups for drawer and message actions (ask design: Keaton).
- 2) Draft simple API spec (ask eng: Mira).
- 3) Run a short survey with internal folks: what would they put in a briefcase? (send to eng/product slack).
- 4) Instrument a telemetry plan for storage and reopens.

Notes-to-self / rough timeline:
- 2 week design spike + API proto, 2 week dogfood, 4 week beta with select customers.
- Watch out for retention policy alignment with legal/compliance (we need legal input early).

Scratch ideas / offhand thoughts:
- Could make "briefcase" a handy offline export (json + zipped attachments) that users can import locally into a private deployment.
- For dedicated customers, allow an admin flag to control whether link-sharing is allowed.
- Offer a one-click redaction step before sharing that scrubs named entities and emails (experimental).

References / related tickets:
- JIRA-5012: session-snapshot-feature — overlapping but heavier; ensure briefcase is lightweight complement.
- GH PR #224: ui/assistant-drawer — reuse some components.
summary: Draft product seed for a lightweight 'Assistant Briefcase' to let users bundle small, portable packages of assistant outputs and context for reuse and sharing. Includes basic user stories, acceptance criteria, metrics, infra sketch, rollout phases, and next steps.
